top.title: No Suspension for Tom Wilson after Hit on Sandis Vilmanis. That’s Wrong
top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Washington Capitals play in Ottawa tonight and Tom Wilson will be in the lineup as if his cheap hit on Florida rookie Sandis Vilmanis never happened. Perhaps we did not see it as well as the NHL’s Department of Player Safety did. Wilson, long one of the NHL’s biggest cheap-shot artists, will not face any sort of supplemental discipline for boarding Vilmanis in the first period of Washington’s 4-3 win over the Panthers on Saturday afternoon. The punishment, we guess, of being kicked out of the game was plenty enough. Wilson has probably learned his lesson. After being suspended six other times, we seriously doubt it. And, based on the language Wilson used on the game officials who tossed him Saturday as he took his sweet time getting to the Washington room, he thought that punishment was too harsh. Really, it was not even close to being enough. Florida coach Paul Maurice was asked about the hit and deferred comment, saying he would “save that for the Department of Player Safety.’’ ”That’s their job,’’ Maurice said. Well, it was not done. Wilson knew full well that Vilmanis was in a vulnerable position along the boards. Vilmanis worked the puck up the ice and Wilson bulldozed him from behind, planting the Florida forward face-first into the dasher boards. There was no doubt it was a boarding call — the puck left Vilmanis’ stick moments before impact — and Wilson had full view of Vilmanis’ number, name plate, and even the small Panthers’ logo on the back of his white helmet. Ever see a young hockey player wearing a jersey to a game and notice the big red stop sign stitched onto the back? It there as a reminder to players not to hit another player in the back. When you see the numbers, stop. Perhaps teams playing the Capitals from now on should put those stop signs on the back of their sweaters. Probably would not help anyway. Vilmanis, 22, missed Sunday’s game in Boston and will likely be out tonight in Columbus as well. Maurice said the Panthers will not know the severity of Vilmanis’ injury until team doctors in Florida get to take a look at him. It is possible Vilmanis skipped the team charter and returned to town. Vilmanis is expected to be fine and he will return to the Florida lineup in time. That is not the point. Wilson has been a dangerous and, based on his 30-plus goals the past two seasons, very talented forward in this league who is now making high-end money. He does not need to keep playing this way to “keep his edge” nor to keep his job. Again, he just needs to do better. Perhaps some day. top.description: Motorsport photo The FIA has announced its final Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) results for the 2026 Formula 1 season, with no changes granted for any of the power unit manufacturers. From this season, the FIA installed a mechanism in the F1 regulations which allowed power unit manufacturers the ability to make updates, if they fell behind the leading engine, in the form of tokens permitted under a performance scale. After the first period in 2026, which ran from the Australian Grand Prix to the Canadian GP, it was announced that Red Bull Ford Powertrains emerged as the benchmark, while Mercedes ’ internal combustion engine trails by between 2-4%, which gave the German manufacturer to one additional upgrade this year and one more next season. Ferrari , Audi and Honda fell into the category of being more than 4% behind on ICE power, which grants them two upgrades during the current campaign and two more in 2027. Red Bull Ford Powertrains asked for a review of the ADUO analysis, which delayed the official publication of the first results, as it disputed the results and being considered the manufacturer with the strongest engine. As agreed before the start of the season by the teams, the FIA only measures the internal combustion engine, but once a manufacturer qualifies for ADUO, it is also allowed to modify electrical components such as the battery and MGU-K. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing So while Red Bull’s rivals have been able to install power unit upgrades across this season, the Milton Keynes-based effort has effectively faced an engine freeze. In the third and final FIA analysis of ADUO – which took engine data from the Dutch GP up to and including the US GP – there has been no change and therefore no manufacturer will gain or lose its current concessions. There was also no change in the second ADUO period over the summer. “For the third period, the relative performance gaps to the leading ICE evolved, but these changes did not result in any additional homologations being granted to the Power Unit Manufacturers,” an FIA report stated. Given the dispute over how ADUO is measured, the FIA is open to changes in the system in the future, subject to approval from the power unit manufacturers, while FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis is confident the concept is working as desired. “The FIA has undertaken extensive analysis as part of the review of ADUO this year. top.title: Kenan Yildiz reveals comeback date as Juventus star prepares to end four month injury nightmare
top.description: Galatasaray-vs-Juventus-Champions-League-2025-26-KO-play-offs-1s - AFP Kenan Yildiz is nearing his highly anticipated return for Juventus after missing several months of action due to injury. The talented forward recently provided a positive update on his recovery, revealing his target date to finally step back onto the pitch this December. Juventus handed major injury boost Yildiz is finally closing in on a return to action for Juventus following a frustrating spell on the sidelines. The 21-year-old has been unavailable due to injury since August , dealing a significant blow to the Italian club. According to Tuttosport , the talented forward will soon resume his individual training programme at the Continassa base. He will then gradually increase his physical workload as he builds up his crucial match fitness. Yildiz will not be ready to feature immediately after the current international break. Juventus are carefully managing his recovery process to ensure he returns in optimal physical condition. Yildiz reveals his comeback timeline The attacker recently attended a ceremony in Bologna on Monday to collect the Bulgarelli Number 8 award. During the event, he provided a highly positive update regarding his ongoing rehabilitation. Yildiz confirmed directly to those in attendance that he expects to be back "in December". The Juventus number 10 expressed his deep desire to get back onto the pitch and contribute alongside his team-mates. "I feel good and I hope to be playing again soon," Yildiz explained when discussing his fitness. "I miss Juventus so much. I miss the feeling of playing football." Coping without the number ten Juventus have been forced to navigate the early months of the campaign without their creative focal point. Despite the lengthy and frustrating absence, Luciano Spalletti has notably refused to use the injury as an excuse. The club and medical staff have now plotted a clear timeline for his gradual reintroduction. A return against Monza on Monday, 14 December at the Allianz Stadium is currently viewed as the most realistic target. Yildiz remains eager to accelerate that process if his body allows it over the next fortnight. The coaching staff will monitor his daily progress closely as he ramps up his training workload. Crucial fixtures await the forward While the Monza fixture remains the primary objective, Juventus are quietly hoping Yildiz could make the matchday squad even sooner. His early availability would provide a timely lift for the busy winter schedule. An accelerated recovery could see him feature in the domestic home game against Udinese on 6 December. Alternatively, he might travel for the Europa League clash against Hapoel Be’er Sheva in Bucharest just four days later. A December return will ultimately provide a massive mid-season boost for Juventus. Yildiz will now focus entirely on completing his individual work at Continassa to make that comeback a reality.

top.title: US reps schedule fresh hearing on ‘Christian persecution’ in Nigeria
top.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The United States House of Representatives is set to hold a congressional hearing on Nigeria’s efforts to protect Christians and tackle insecurity in the Middle Belt, with Republican lawmaker Chris Smith leading the session on Thursday, November 12. According to a statement issued by Smith’s office on Monday, the session is titled ‘One Year Later: Assessing Nigeria’s Efforts to Protect Christians and Secure the Middle Belt’, with hearing scheduled for 11am at the Rayburn House Office Building in Washington, DC. It partly reads, “Congressional hearing that assesses the current state of religious violence perpetrated by radical Islamists, such as Boko Haram and Fulani terrorists, against Christians in Nigeria; the Nigerian government’s efforts to curb the persecution and punish those responsible for committing atrocities against Christian and non-radical Muslim communities; and the steps the United States can take to ensure that Nigerian officials are addressing and preventing the systemic violence against Christians and non-radical Muslims by Islamist extremists.” The first panel will feature Frank Garcia, Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs, and Riley Barnes, Assistant Secretary of State for Democracy, Human Rights and Labour. The second panel will include Nina Shea, senior fellow and director of the Centre for Religious Freedom at the Hudson Institute; Ryan Brown, chief executive officer of Open Doors US; and Oge Onubogu, director and senior fellow of the Africa Programme at the Centre for Strategic and International Studies. The hearing will be streamed live on YouTube. This will be Smith’s 14th congressional hearing exclusively on Nigeria. In November 2025, he chaired a hearing after President Donald Trump’s redesignation of Nigeria as a ‘country of particular concern’. In May 2016, he also chaired a hearing on “The U.S. role in helping Nigeria confront Boko Haram and other threats in northern Nigeria.” The post US reps schedule fresh hearing on ‘Christian persecution’ in Nigeria appeared first on Vanguard News .

top.title: Barcelona defender Cubarsi named 2026 Golden Boy winner
top.description: Barcelona defender Cubarsi named 2026 Golden Boy winner Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsí has won the 2026 Golden Boy award, given to the best Under-21 men’s player in the world. The 19-year-old succeeds Paris Saint-Germain forward Désiré Doué and becomes the fourth Barcelona player to win the prize in the last six years. Cubarsí follows in the footsteps of team-mates Pedri, Gavi and Lamine Yamal, who have all previously claimed the award. He is also the first defender to win the Golden Boy since Matthijs de Ligt, then of Ajax, was named the winner in 2018. The award was established by Italian sports newspaper Tuttosport in 2003 and has previously been won by some of the biggest names in world football. nigeria.title: US reps schedule fresh hearing on ‘Christian persecution’ in Nigeria
nigeria.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The United States House of Representatives is set to hold a congressional hearing on Nigeria’s efforts to protect Christians and tackle insecurity in the Middle Belt, with Republican lawmaker Chris Smith leading the session on Thursday, November 12. According to a statement issued by Smith’s office on Monday, the session is titled ‘One Year Later: Assessing Nigeria’s Efforts to Protect Christians and Secure the Middle Belt’, with hearing scheduled for 11am at the Rayburn House Office Building in Washington, DC. It partly reads, “Congressional hearing that assesses the current state of religious violence perpetrated by radical Islamists, such as Boko Haram and Fulani terrorists, against Christians in Nigeria; the Nigerian government’s efforts to curb the persecution and punish those responsible for committing atrocities against Christian and non-radical Muslim communities; and the steps the United States can take to ensure that Nigerian officials are addressing and preventing the systemic violence against Christians and non-radical Muslims by Islamist extremists.” The first panel will feature Frank Garcia, Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs, and Riley Barnes, Assistant Secretary of State for Democracy, Human Rights and Labour. The second panel will include Nina Shea, senior fellow and director of the Centre for Religious Freedom at the Hudson Institute; Ryan Brown, chief executive officer of Open Doors US; and Oge Onubogu, director and senior fellow of the Africa Programme at the Centre for Strategic and International Studies. The hearing will be streamed live on YouTube. This will be Smith’s 14th congressional hearing exclusively on Nigeria. nigeria.title: Carrick set to be sacked by Man Utd: reports
nigeria.description: Michael Carrick is set to be sacked by Manchester United after his side’s dismal start to the season, according to reports on Tuesday. United’s hierarchy have been conducting an internal review of the club’s miserable form and it is believed that Carrick will shortly be relieved of his duties. United are in the midst of their worst opening to a campaign in 40 years, leaving them languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after an eight-match winless run. Although it is said that no final decision has been made, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are reportedly leaning towards dismissing Carrick. United owners the Glazer family and influential shareholder Jim Ratcliffe would then decide whether to act on that recommendation. Carrick was seen arriving at United’s Carrington training base on Tuesday, but it appears to be only a matter of time before his turbulent reign comes to an end. The 45-year-old, hired on a permanent basis in the close season after a successful interim spell last term, had been granted a stay of execution after he was widely expected to be axed in late October following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth. United’s surprise decision to let Carrick limp on failed to produce a significant improvement in performances, particularly defensively. They were beaten 2-0 at Chelsea, then scrambled a last-gasp 3-2 win against Roma in the Champions League after falling two goals down. It looked certain that former United midfielder Carrick would be on the way out when his team twice trailed by two goals against Aston Villa on Sunday. When United scored twice in stoppage-time to rescue an improbable 4-4 draw, it was interpreted as a positive sign for Carrick as the players were still fighting for him. But United’s powerbrokers look set to make yet another managerial change in a bid to avoid being dragged into an embarrassing relegation battle. USA boss Mauricio Pochettino, former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe, ex-Chelsea chief Antonio Conte and former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann have all been linked with the United job. United have the rest of the two-week international break to secure a replacement for Carrick before returning to action at bitter rivals Liverpool on November 22. nigeria.description: A US judge has ordered a psychiatric examination for Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Prince Harry’s wife, Meghan Markle, after his arrest for alleged possession of images of child sexual abuse. Thomas Markle, 82, is charged with one count of “possession of child pornography” and made an initial court appearance in Tampa in Florida on Friday. Judge Lindsay Griffin cited his “health condition,” “advanced age” and “lack of recall” in the order issued on Friday, without providing further details. Markle was taken into custody by FBI agents earlier that day at the retirement home where he lives in Lakeland, Florida. The Justice Department said he allegedly “kept child sexual abuse material (CSAM), including sexually explicit photographs of himself with prepubescent girls, in two Los Angeles-area storage units he rented for nearly two decades.” File photo of Meghan and Thomas Markle Pictures of child sex abuse have also allegedly been found at Markle’s former home in the Philippines and at a storage unit he rented in Mexico. nigeria.title: French Students Block Dozens Of Schools
nigeria.description: French students blocked the entrances to dozens of high schools on Tuesday, the education ministry said, as they kept up protests for better learning conditions. Student protests across France since September have spiraled into larger cost-of-living demonstrations in recent weeks, some marked by fringe violence and accusations of police brutality. The unrest comes ahead of elections to replace President Emmanuel Macron next year. With the European Union’s second biggest economy under pressure to rein in debt, the government has limited scope to appease protesters through additional spending. Students dance in front of police officers during a rally over learning conditions as part of a nationwide day of action, as unions hold strikes alongside student-led demonstrations that have gripped the country for weeks in Paris on November 5, 2026. Forty-nine of the country’s 3,700 high schools for 15- to 18-year-olds were blockaded on Tuesday morning, the ministry said. Authorities expected several thousand school and university students at a Paris protest on Tuesday afternoon. “Now is the time to step up the mobilisation by continuing to put pressure on the government,” student and teacher unions said in a joint statement released Monday. Student association leader Ryad Rani said it was essential to keep up the pressure. “We’re not just fighting for ourselves. We’re fighting for teachers, for their working conditions,” he said. The government has announced measures including the gradual replacement of an online selection platform to access higher education, as well as financial means for some of the worst-off schools. But students say this is not enough. Unions are not happy either, with one leader saying on Monday that a government pledge to increase the minimum wage by 0.6 percent on top of a standard adjustment for inflation was “crumbs”. They have called for a new day of strikes and protests on November 17. Around 575,000 people demonstrated across the country during cost-of-living strikes and protests last Thursday, according to authorities. Unions put the number at 1.5 million. nigeria.title: Iran calls on US to meet its demands to end war
nigeria.description: Iran on Tuesday urged the United States to meet its demands in a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, after President Donald Trump spoke of “positive momentum” to end their eight-month war. “The conflict with Iran will not be resolved through military means, nor by intensifying sanctions,” Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Iran’s IRNA news agency. “The only solution is to adopt a language of respect, engage in diplomacy, and address Iran’s demands and conditions — which were outlined in the two-day proposal and remain on the table.” Tehran has proposed reopening Hormuz, which it has blockaded since the start of the war, within two days in return for Washington meeting a raft of conditions. These include ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the US counter-blockade of Iranian ports. Trump, whose Republican party last week lost midterm elections in part due to the war, said on Monday that there was “positive momentum” towards ending the conflict after meeting Qatar’s prime minister at the White House. In a post on social media, Trump reiterated that the US was “locked and loaded” but said further strikes were “quite unlikely” given that key US allies in the Gulf “would prefer the status quo”. “We are seeing positive momentum toward an end to this conflict, and will ensure that America’s interests are at all times protected,” Trump said. Diplomatic efforts, led by Qatar and Pakistan, are underway to find a resolution to the war, which broke out in late February when US-Israeli strikes killed Iran’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. On Tuesday, Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei urged Washington to “surrender” to the Iranian demands. “The war on Iran has already wrecked the US government. But Washington flails like a desperate gambler. FOLD YOUR HAND. STOP manufacturing FAKE NEWS about imaginary talks,” said Rezaei, the head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, in a post on X. nigeria.title: Nigeria’s active telecom lines hit 200m as 5G share crosses 5%
nigeria.description: …As Internet data usage falls to 1.73 terabytes in September By Juliet Umeh Nigeria’s active telecommunications subscriptions rose to 200.3 million in September, crossing the 200 million mark for the first time since the NIN-SIM enforcement exercise led to mass line disconnections in 2024. Latest data from the Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC, showed that active lines increased by about 2.9 million, from 197.4 million in August. The September figure of 200,337,097 subscriptions was up from 197,416,694 in August. Teledensity rose to 92.41 per cent from 91.07 per cent. The NCC defines teledensity as the number of active telephone connections per 100 inhabitants. It measures subscriptions rather than unique users, as one person may have more than one line. The data showed that 4G remained the largest share of mobile connections at 54.37 per cent in September. 2G accounted for 36.42 per cent, while 3G made up 4.16 per cent. 5G’s share increased to 5.05 per cent from 4.92 per cent in August. Internet subscriptions also grew, rising to 160.9 million from 158.5 million in August. Broadband subscriptions increased to 128 million in September from 126.2 million the previous month, while broadband penetration rose to 59.05 per cent from 58.22 per cent. However, total internet data usage declined to 1.73 million terabytes in September from 1.76 million terabytes in August. Mobile number porting increased during the month, with 1,603 subscribers switching networks, compared with 1,111 in August. MTN recorded 854 incoming ports, Airtel 580, Globacom 165 and Vitel four. T2 recorded none. The figures also showed that the telecommunications industry’s contribution to gross domestic product, GDP, rose to 9.72 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 from 9.19 per cent in the first quarter. Fixed broadband infrastructure expanded, with Fibre to the X (FTTX) subscriptions rising to 401,666 in the third quarter from 319,735 in the second quarter. The NCC’s FTTX category covers fibre connections to homes, offices, streets, hubs and other locations, including subscriptions from internet service providers and fixed or private network operators. nigeria.title: New Israel parliament to be sworn in as Eisenkot seeks government
nigeria.description: Israel’s new parliament will be sworn in Tuesday, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu set to lose his majority even as rival Gadi Eisenkot still works to form a new government. President Isaac Herzog will deliver a speech at 4:00 pm (1400 GMT) for the swearing-in of the 120-seat parliament, in which neither Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc nor Eisenkot’s opposition will hold a majority. The opposition hopes to use its newfound legislative power to move quickly on key priorities, including a commission to investigate security failures under Netanyahu that allowed the October 7, 2023 attack by Hamas, the deadliest day in Israel’s history. Herzog on Sunday gave Eisenkot the initial mandate to form a government, starting the clock for him to cobble together a coalition within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension. Ahead of the parliament opening, Eisenkot’s party announced progress in naming people to seek key positions. The opposition will put forward Matan Kahana — like Eisenkot a former senior military figure — as speaker of the parliament, Eisenkot’s Yashar party said. Avigdor Lieberman, a right-wing opposition leader who has played a key role in deciding who can enter the government, will be nominated as chair of the foreign affairs and defence committee. The opposition’s choice for speaker would need to secure a larger number of votes than anyone backed by Netanyahu’s bloc, which has been trying to push back a vote on the speaker. The newly formed government would need 61 votes to be approved to take office. Eisenkot could secure the threshold with support from Arab-Israeli lawmakers, who secured a record number of seats on the back of anger in the minority community over Netanyahu’s hard-right government. But Lieberman had been clear he would not allow Eisenkot to rely on Arab-Israelis to come to power. He has instead proposed an alliance with ultra-Orthodox Jews, despite his years of bitter denunciations of the community for its singular priority on maintaining an exemption from mandatory military service. Eisenkot’s core opposition bloc has fewer seats than Netanyahu at 48, but would achieve a majority if the 19 Arab-Israeli lawmakers either enter the government or, more likely, vote for it without joining. The two ultra-Orthodox parties, with 13 seats, could also crown Eisenkot if they ditch their long alliance with Netanyahu, who backed the exemption from military service without enshrining it fully into law. An alliance with either group would likely be fragile. Arab-Israelis are likely to object if Eisenkot carries out another major offensive in Gaza. Eisenkot has largely backed Netanyahu’s war decisions, although he has vowed to crack down on extremist settlers in the West Bank who have been attacking and stealing from Palestinians with virtual impunity. nigeria.title: Rwandan author urges readers to turn knowledge into wisdom
nigeria.description: Rwandan author, entrepreneur and cultural advocate, Lisa Munezero, has said self-awareness, resilience, discipline and purposeful action can influence the direction of people’s lives, saying individuals must look beyond conventional definitions of success. Munezero also warned that qualifications, ambition and access to opportunities alone do not guarantee fulfilment. The author stated this in the book: ‘The Well of Knowing: 8 Lessons of Becoming,’ set to be unveiled at a public presentation on November 14, 2026, at 1:00 p.m., at Four Points by Sheraton, Victoria Island, Lagos, Nigeria. Attendance is by invitation. The publication introduces eight interconnected lessons exploring the relationship between knowledge, personal development, purposeful living and the decisions that shape individual achievement. Its central proposition is that what people do with what they know shapes the opportunities they create and the people they become. Drawing on entrepreneurial experiences, personal reflections and practical wisdom, Munezero invites readers to look beyond conventional definitions of success and consider how self-awareness, resilience, discipline and purposeful action can influence the direction of their lives. The Well of Knowing asks how individuals discover purpose, learn from rejection and failure, turn ideas into opportunities, and transform acquired knowledge into wisdom, influence and lasting contributions to society. Addressing students, aspiring entrepreneurs, professionals and emerging leaders, the book presents personal development as an ongoing journey. It also explores mentorship, relationships and responsible leadership as ways in which individual growth can benefit communities and future generations. In his foreword, teacher, poet, dramatist and founder of Step Out Creatives Publications in the United Kingdom, Dr Isi Agboaye, highlights the book’s emphasis on purpose and action and draws a comparison with Norman Vincent Peale’s The Power of Positive Thinking. Senior banking professional and author of Threads of Love and Duty, Aderonke Adeyinka, recommends the publication to aspiring entrepreneurs and readers interested in personal growth, recognizing its attention to resilience and lifelong learning. nigeria.title: UFC chief declines Trump’s White House job offer
nigeria.description: Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief Dana White turned down President Donald Trump’s — apparently jovial — offer of a job as press secretary in a surprise appearance at the White House on Monday. Trump stunned the world by saying on social media on Saturday that he had asked White to take on the high-profile post — but a day later the 80-year-old president said he was “only kidding.” The 57-year-old cage fighting boss visited the White House on Monday, and Trump brought him out for a chaotic news conference in the James Brady Briefing Room. “So let me ask you the big question. Would you like to be press secretary of the United States of America? Or do you just want to stay with this ridiculous UFC? Huh?” Trump said. “Thank you for the offer, sir — for the offer, I have no, no — I do not want to be in politics,” White replied. Trump smiled and headed out of the room, saying: “I am devastated to hear this. Goodbye, everybody.” The press secretary’s post has been been vacant since Katie Zacharia left on October 16 after less than a week in the post. Her combative predecessor Karoline Leavitt left in August after a year and a half in the job. Trump’s announcement that he had offered the high-profile job to “violent Fighter and Warrior” White had sparked speculation that he was ready for a aggressive stance after the Republican Party’s stunning midterm elections defeat. White is a long-time friend of the president and helped host a massive UFC match on the White House lawn earlier this year. But there was also some skepticism about the president’s announcement, and Trump said Sunday night that he had been joking. – ‘Beat the hell out of you’ – Leading out White to the podium on Monday, Trump said he had been “having a little fun.” “He’s a great guy,” Trump told the room full of reporters. “The only problem is he’ll talk for a little while and then he’s going to beat the hell out of you.” Standing at the lectern and wearing a black t-shirt and jacket, White looked like he might be more comfortable in the octagon — the ring used for UFC fights. “I’ve always wanted to do this. Who has the first question?” he joked — before quickliy adding: “I have zero political aspirations.” White added that “the last 24 hours of my life has been insane” since Trump made the announcement. Asked by a journalist to confirm he had said no to the job, White added: “I don’t tell the president ‘no’ to anything… I didn’t want to be disrespectful and say anything until he said something first.” Trump then took a series of questions on more weighty matters, from the Iran and Ukraine wars to the possible impeachment of Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth and a spy scandal engulfing Nvidia boss Jensen Huang. nigeria.title: N10m reward to motivate FCT councillors, not vote buying — APC chair defends Wike
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, Nentawe Yilwatda, has defended the N10 million reward promised by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, to councillors who deliver their wards for President Bola Tinubu and other APC candidates in the 2027 general elections. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today, on Monday, Yilwatda said the money was intended to motivate councillors and would be paid after the election, once the result had been established. “He was speaking to the FCT councillors in the forum, and I’m sure it’s addressing something about 62 or 60-something councillors in the FCT,” he said. Asked whether the offer amounted to voter inducement, Yilwatda rejected the suggestion, arguing that political parties routinely provide funds for mobilisation. “Which political party doesn’t release money for mobilisation? Which political party? So, tell me one. No, it’s not for votes. The same reward for you to deliver Tinubu in your ward,” he said. Yilwatda compared the offer to rewarding students for academic achievement but maintained that the timing of the payment was significant. “The money is not given before the election. It doesn’t matter? No, it matters. It matters because if the money is given after the election has been concluded and the winner has been declared and there’s nothing at stake again—if the court has proven and all the legal rules have been followed—that you legally deliver your ward by giving you N10 million,” he said. Asked again whether he considered the offer of vote buying, Yilwatda replied authoritatively: “Never.” Wike made the pledge at a political meeting in Kwali Area Council, promising N10 million to each councillor who delivers their ward for Tinubu and the APC in 2027. Asked whether the APC would return Godswill Akpabio as Senate President if he wins re-election, Yilwatda said the decision would rest with senators. “Let’s wait for the election first. I don’t have anybody in mind. The Senate will determine who they want to make the Senate President,” he said. On reports of electoral violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, Yilwatda said he sympathised with anyone injured and said the APC supported free and fair elections. “If anybody is injured by anybody across the country, I’m sure it shouldn’t be by APC supporters. I pity anybody who is being injured, and I sympathise with them. Our party stands for free and fair elections,” he said. nigeria.title: Trump sees ‘positive momentum’ on Iran after Qatar PM talks
nigeria.description: US President Donald Trump said on Monday there was momentum toward ending the war with Iran, as he declared that the country “militarily, is effectively over,” but kept open the possibility of new strikes. nigeria.title: I give kudos to people who sent me to jail; it’s like school – Orji Kalu
nigeria.description: Senator representing Abia North, Orji Kalu, has praised those responsible for his imprisonment, saying the six months he spent behind bars gave him valuable life lessons and made him a more humble person. Kalu said rather than regret his incarceration, he considers it an experience that changed his understanding of life and helped him develop a different outlook. The former Abia State governor made the remarks during an interview on Arise Television on Monday. Explaining why he was grateful for the experience, Kalu said, “It made me more humble. It made me to realise that life is not the same thing I used to think about. So I’m very grateful to God I was there.” He added, “And I gave kudos to people that sent me there because it’s like going to school. And I graduated there, and I’m very happy I went there.” Kalu was convicted by a Federal High Court in Lagos in December 2019 on a 39-count charge and sentenced to 12 years’ imprisonment. However, the Supreme Court overturned the conviction on May 8, 2020, ruling that the trial judge, Mohammed Idris, lacked jurisdiction to deliver the judgment after his elevation to the Court of Appeal. The apex court ordered a fresh trial, and Kalu was released from Kuje Correctional Centre after spending approximately six months in custody. Asked whether he believed the conviction was justified, the senator disagreed but said he did not wish to dwell on the matter. “No, it wasn’t the right thing to do. But I don’t like to discuss this because the judge had his reasons. When the judge did it, I praised him. I support all his decisions,” he said. Kalu also acknowledged that the judiciary had its challenges but maintained that some judges remained committed to dispensing justice. He advised Nigerians dissatisfied with rulings of lower courts to pursue appeals rather than publicly condemn judicial decisions. According to him, taking cases to higher courts gives litigants another opportunity to obtain justice, as more judges are involved in reviewing the decisions. Speaking on the theme “Losing the Fear” , at The International Women Leadership Conference (TIWLC) in Dubai, organised by the Ibukun Awosika Leadership Foundation, Ekeh , who was a keynote speaker on the final day of this year’s conference, addressed over 600 women industry leaders from different countries across the globe. entertainment.title: Nkanyeziyethu Malunga: The Zimbabwean Designer Preserving African Heritage Through Fashion
entertainment.description: At her workshop in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, Nkanyeziyethu Malunga crafted colour into fabric, using plants, tree bark and other natural materials gathered from the environment. Choosing a colour or designing a pattern is only one of the processes. Each material carries details on how it was gathered, prepared, and transformed, which Malunga is incorporating into contemporary fashion. “My dyes are mainly extracted from plants such as mnyii and hibiscus. Although I also use many other plants, including tubers, that have properties suitable for dye extraction. I love hibiscus not only for its petals, which produce beautiful dyes, but also for its tea.” The 37-year-old designer is challenging conventional notions about what defines a fashion collection and where creative knowledge originates. Through her clothing business, GANU, she transforms indigenous materials and skills into clothes and accessories, demonstrating how knowledge passed down through generations can inform modern design, provide opportunities for rural women, and conserve cultural practices. Her method is based on teachings learned from her late maternal grandmother, Ngatsha Nkatha, who resided in Tsholotsho, a rural district in Zimbabwe. During the school vacations, Malunga and her siblings traveled from Bulawayo to visit grandma, witnessing as she turned sisal, sedge, and reeds into winnowing baskets. “When I was a child, I often visited my grandmother in the village with my siblings. She was very dexterous with her fingers, and that passion eventually became mutual.” Malunga started experimenting with fashion in her teens before launching Ganu in 2013. The name is derived from iganu, the Ndebele term for marula fruit, and represents her connection to local resources and African identity. Her creations blend basketry, crocheting, batik, and beadwork with natural dyes, leather, and other locally produced materials. For Malunga, the importance of these materials goes beyond their appearance. Bamboo, sisal, reeds, and sedge are used in basketry, and she breeds Angora goats for their fur, which she straightens and dyes to make garments. Cowhide obtained from local abattoirs is softened in a tannery before being mixed into leather designs. “I keep Angora goats for the fur needed in garment production. However, for raw materials such as cowhide, I usually source these from local abattoirs while sisal and tree barks are either harvested by me or sometimes extracted by colleagues I work with, who are based in the rural areas.” Desmond Ntini , a cultural entrepreneur based in Bulawayo, sees Malunga’s work as part of a broader shift in how African history is perceived and used. ” Malunga is redefining the fashion industry by blending traditional African influences with contemporary creativity. entertainment.title: Israel Olaleye: What Selling Land Taught Me About How Nigerians Think About Money
entertainment.description: In 2021, I graduated from the University of Ibadan with a degree in Mathematics. I thought my life would be about numbers on a whiteboard. I did not know it would become about numbers in people’s bank accounts, and the fears, hopes and contradictions that sit behind them. By mid-2023, I had taken a job selling real estate. I started at the very bottom, as a sales development representative: the person who makes the first call, sends the message and follows up when nobody replies. Today, I manage a sales team. Somewhere between then and now, I stopped seeing real estate as a business of land and buildings. I started seeing it as a mirror. Put a property in front of a Nigerian, and you will learn, very quickly, how they think about money. Here is some of what that mirror has shown me: A prospect once told me, with complete confidence, “I have my money ready for the land.” We fixed an inspection. We walked the site together under the afternoon sun, red earth on our shoes. Then, standing on the plot, the prospect asked if they could pay next year. I was not angry. I understood. Saying “I am ready” feels good. Being ready is different. It means you have decided what the money is for, and you are willing to let it go. I have seen versions of that moment many times. The client who books an inspection for 2 pm and is still not there at 4 pm. The person who asks for options, receives ten properties that match exactly what they requested, and replies, “Do you have something else?” The buyer who is ready until it is time to decide, and then needs three more months to think. The one who disappeared after asking for a price came back after the price went up, and asked for the old price. For a long time, these moments frustrated me. But they taught me that most people do not have a money problem. They have a decision problem. We are a generation that earns, spends, plans and postpones, often all at the same time. You can earn a lot and still not be wealthy One idea I keep returning to is that you can earn twenty million naira a year and still not be wealthy. Income is what comes in. Wealth is what stays and grows. Two people can earn the same salary and end up in completely different places ten years later, simply because one converted part of that income into assets and the other converted all of it into lifestyle. Wealthy people do not always look wealthy. Some of the most financially secure people I have met do not drive the loudest cars. And some of the people who look the richest are one bad month away from panic. So the question I now ask myself, and the people I speak with, is simple: what exactly are you converting your income into? From the era when a four-hundred-million-Naira milestone set the nationwide ceiling to an era defined by multi-billion-Naira theatrical runs, audiences across West Africa continue to show up in massive numbers for homegrown storytelling. sports.title: No Suspension for Tom Wilson after Hit on Sandis Vilmanis. That’s Wrong
sports.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Washington Capitals play in Ottawa tonight and Tom Wilson will be in the lineup as if his cheap hit on Florida rookie Sandis Vilmanis never happened. Perhaps we did not see it as well as the NHL’s Department of Player Safety did. Wilson, long one of the NHL’s biggest cheap-shot artists, will not face any sort of supplemental discipline for boarding Vilmanis in the first period of Washington’s 4-3 win over the Panthers on Saturday afternoon. The punishment, we guess, of being kicked out of the game was plenty enough. Wilson has probably learned his lesson. After being suspended six other times, we seriously doubt it. And, based on the language Wilson used on the game officials who tossed him Saturday as he took his sweet time getting to the Washington room, he thought that punishment was too harsh. Really, it was not even close to being enough. Florida coach Paul Maurice was asked about the hit and deferred comment, saying he would “save that for the Department of Player Safety.’’ ”That’s their job,’’ Maurice said. Well, it was not done. Wilson knew full well that Vilmanis was in a vulnerable position along the boards. Vilmanis worked the puck up the ice and Wilson bulldozed him from behind, planting the Florida forward face-first into the dasher boards. There was no doubt it was a boarding call — the puck left Vilmanis’ stick moments before impact — and Wilson had full view of Vilmanis’ number, name plate, and even the small Panthers’ logo on the back of his white helmet. Ever see a young hockey player wearing a jersey to a game and notice the big red stop sign stitched onto the back? It there as a reminder to players not to hit another player in the back. When you see the numbers, stop. Perhaps teams playing the Capitals from now on should put those stop signs on the back of their sweaters. Probably would not help anyway. Vilmanis, 22, missed Sunday’s game in Boston and will likely be out tonight in Columbus as well. Maurice said the Panthers will not know the severity of Vilmanis’ injury until team doctors in Florida get to take a look at him. It is possible Vilmanis skipped the team charter and returned to town. Vilmanis is expected to be fine and he will return to the Florida lineup in time. That is not the point. Wilson has been a dangerous and, based on his 30-plus goals the past two seasons, very talented forward in this league who is now making high-end money. He does not need to keep playing this way to “keep his edge” nor to keep his job. Again, he just needs to do better. Perhaps some day. sports.title: FIA reveals latest ADUO results in final review of 2026 F1 season
sports.description: Motorsport photo The FIA has announced its final Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) results for the 2026 Formula 1 season, with no changes granted for any of the power unit manufacturers. From this season, the FIA installed a mechanism in the F1 regulations which allowed power unit manufacturers the ability to make updates, if they fell behind the leading engine, in the form of tokens permitted under a performance scale. After the first period in 2026, which ran from the Australian Grand Prix to the Canadian GP, it was announced that Red Bull Ford Powertrains emerged as the benchmark, while Mercedes ’ internal combustion engine trails by between 2-4%, which gave the German manufacturer to one additional upgrade this year and one more next season. Ferrari , Audi and Honda fell into the category of being more than 4% behind on ICE power, which grants them two upgrades during the current campaign and two more in 2027. Red Bull Ford Powertrains asked for a review of the ADUO analysis, which delayed the official publication of the first results, as it disputed the results and being considered the manufacturer with the strongest engine. As agreed before the start of the season by the teams, the FIA only measures the internal combustion engine, but once a manufacturer qualifies for ADUO, it is also allowed to modify electrical components such as the battery and MGU-K. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing So while Red Bull’s rivals have been able to install power unit upgrades across this season, the Milton Keynes-based effort has effectively faced an engine freeze. In the third and final FIA analysis of ADUO – which took engine data from the Dutch GP up to and including the US GP – there has been no change and therefore no manufacturer will gain or lose its current concessions. There was also no change in the second ADUO period over the summer. “For the third period, the relative performance gaps to the leading ICE evolved, but these changes did not result in any additional homologations being granted to the Power Unit Manufacturers,” an FIA report stated. Given the dispute over how ADUO is measured, the FIA is open to changes in the system in the future, subject to approval from the power unit manufacturers, while FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis is confident the concept is working as desired. “The FIA has undertaken extensive analysis as part of the review of ADUO this year. Based on the quality of the data and the robustness of the assessment process, we are confident in our findings and the conclusions reached,” Tombazis said. sports.description: Galatasaray-vs-Juventus-Champions-League-2025-26-KO-play-offs-1s - AFP Kenan Yildiz is nearing his highly anticipated return for Juventus after missing several months of action due to injury. The talented forward recently provided a positive update on his recovery, revealing his target date to finally step back onto the pitch this December. Juventus handed major injury boost Yildiz is finally closing in on a return to action for Juventus following a frustrating spell on the sidelines. The 21-year-old has been unavailable due to injury since August , dealing a significant blow to the Italian club. According to Tuttosport , the talented forward will soon resume his individual training programme at the Continassa base. He will then gradually increase his physical workload as he builds up his crucial match fitness. Yildiz will not be ready to feature immediately after the current international break. Juventus are carefully managing his recovery process to ensure he returns in optimal physical condition. Yildiz reveals his comeback timeline The attacker recently attended a ceremony in Bologna on Monday to collect the Bulgarelli Number 8 award. During the event, he provided a highly positive update regarding his ongoing rehabilitation. Yildiz confirmed directly to those in attendance that he expects to be back "in December". The Juventus number 10 expressed his deep desire to get back onto the pitch and contribute alongside his team-mates. "I feel good and I hope to be playing again soon," Yildiz explained when discussing his fitness. "I miss Juventus so much. I miss the feeling of playing football." Coping without the number ten Juventus have been forced to navigate the early months of the campaign without their creative focal point. Despite the lengthy and frustrating absence, Luciano Spalletti has notably refused to use the injury as an excuse. The club and medical staff have now plotted a clear timeline for his gradual reintroduction. A return against Monza on Monday, 14 December at the Allianz Stadium is currently viewed as the most realistic target. Yildiz remains eager to accelerate that process if his body allows it over the next fortnight. The coaching staff will monitor his daily progress closely as he ramps up his training workload. Crucial fixtures await the forward While the Monza fixture remains the primary objective, Juventus are quietly hoping Yildiz could make the matchday squad even sooner. His early availability would provide a timely lift for the busy winter schedule. An accelerated recovery could see him feature in the domestic home game against Udinese on 6 December. Alternatively, he might travel for the Europa League clash against Hapoel Be’er Sheva in Bucharest just four days later. A December return will ultimately provide a massive mid-season boost for Juventus. Yildiz will now focus entirely on completing his individual work at Continassa to make that comeback a reality.

sports.title: Barcelona defender Cubarsi named 2026 Golden Boy winner
sports.description: Barcelona defender Cubarsi named 2026 Golden Boy winner Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsí has won the 2026 Golden Boy award, given to the best Under-21 men’s player in the world. The 19-year-old succeeds Paris Saint-Germain forward Désiré Doué and becomes the fourth Barcelona player to win the prize in the last six years. Cubarsí follows in the footsteps of team-mates Pedri, Gavi and Lamine Yamal, who have all previously claimed the award. He is also the first defender to win the Golden Boy since Matthijs de Ligt, then of Ajax, was named the winner in 2018. The award was established by Italian sports newspaper Tuttosport in 2003 and has previously been won by some of the biggest names in world football. Erling Haaland, Kylian Mbappé and Lionel Messi are among the former recipients of the prize.

Is the end of Impact Player rule a reason behind franchises opting for all-rounders over specialists originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: The only completed four-player swap of this window sent two seamers out and brought two all-rounders in. Hardik Pandya is set to join PBKS, while Sam Curran and Romario Shepherd have all been linked with moves. Reports suggest the Impact Player rule could be scrapped after IPL 2027 season. Why are IPL teams going for all-rounders in this trade window? Chennai Super Kings made the most interesting move of this window when they sent Khaleel Ahmed and Nathan Ellis, two specialist seamers, to Sunrisers Hyderabad, and took all-rounders Liam Livingstone and Jack Edwards in exchange. The most talked-about move of the IPL 2027 trade window also involves an all-rounder, as India star Hardik Pandya is set to join Punjab Kings. Both MI and Punjab are set to confirm that Pandya left Mumbai on Tuesday, while Arshdeep came the other way. Defending champions Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Rajasthan Royals have also been discussing a Romario Shepherd-for-Sam Curran swap, which is a like-for-like trade. Set against the three seasons that preceded it, there is clearly a reverse trend. Since 2023, squads have been built around specialists because of the Impact Player rule, which allowed teams to add an extra player in between matches. MORE: Hardik Pandya-Arshdeep Singh trade: What do MI and PBKS stand to gain from the deal Will the IPL Impact player rule be scrapped? The future of the Impact player rule has been under review since the conclusion of the IPL 2026 campaign. The BCCI wrote to all ten franchises seeking formal feedback before the August 31 deadline, and the subject came up again at the IPL Governing Council meeting , with chairman Arun Dhumal saying only that the matter was under discussion and a call would follow after consulting stakeholders. Sachin Tendulkar urged the board to drop it. Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Hardik Pandya, Axar Patel and Shubman Gill have all raised the same objection: that the rule devalues genuine all-rounders by letting teams field a specialist for every job. The board's own behaviour has been contradictory. In late September 2024, it confirmed the Impact Player would run through the 2025-2027 cycle. Two weeks later, it scrapped the rule from the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, the competition that was used to trial it in the first place. According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, via CalcioMercato , the former full-back looked back on a career that took him from Venezia to Juventus, Sampdoria, Fiorentina, Atlético Madrid, Parma and finally Inter, the club he supported as a boy. He joined Sampdoria from Juventus as part of the deal that took Gianluca Vialli to Turin. “Roberto Mancini? Very good, but unbearable,” Serena said. “I argued with him in my first year, and Mantovani fined him and took my side. Vierchowod told me to apologise to Mancini, so after one training session I locked him in a small room with me until we finally sorted things out. After that, we built a good relationship, and we still speak today.” BURSA, TURKEY – SEPTEMBER 28: Roberto Mancini, Head Coach of Italy, looks on before the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Türkiye and Italy at Atatürk Spor Kompleksi Matli Stadyumu on September 28, 2026 in Bursa, Turkey. (Photo by Ahmad Mora/Getty Images) Serena on Mancini, Mihajlović and Batistuta Sinisa Mihajlović was another Sampdoria teammate, and he used to make Serena go in goal. “After training, Mihajlović would put me in goal and take free-kicks. It would finish 20-0 or 20-1 to him.” At Fiorentina, Serena played alongside Gabriel Batistuta and Rui Costa. “Bati was the most complete No 9 I’ve ever seen. With Rui, we always wondered how he could smoke so many cigarettes and then run like that on the pitch. “Edmundo? I’ll never forgive him for not coming back from the Rio Carnival. Mandatory Credit: Allsport UK /Allsport Serena finished his career at Inter in 2003, but he’s still haunted by 5 May 2002. On the final day of that season, Héctor Cúper’s side lost 4-2 at Lazio, and Juventus took the title. “I wanted to retire by winning the Scudetto with Inter, the team I’ve supported since I was a child. Instead, on that 5 May, I don’t know what happened… It’s a wound that’s still open, and it still hurts too much today. “I was supposed to play that day instead of Gresko. I’d done everything to recover from an injury, but Cúper changed his mind at the last minute. I confronted him about it, because not playing that day really hurt me.”

"It is with deep sadness and broken hearts that we announce the passing of our beloved Izzy, surrounded by her closest family and friends," a joint statement from the family and Racing NSW said. The rest of the Cotton Cup meeting was abandoned and Neale's horse Marnoo was euthanised after sustaining a serious leg injury in the accident. A second rider, Diego Montes de Oca, was injured in the same race. He suffered minor injuries to his foot and has since been discharged from hospital. Neale was an apprentice rider and rode 88 winners in her professional career. The Australian Turf club described Neale as a "talented young rider with a bright future". technology.title: EU's €212M border IT project lands IBM and Atos in legal water
technology.description: The European Union has dragged IBM, Atos, and Leonardo into court over years of delays to its troubled €212 million smart border system, which finally went live after missing a string of deadlines and leaving travelers stuck in airport queues. The lawsuit dates back to December 22, 2025, when eu-LISA, the agency behind the EU's fingerprint-and-facial-image border checks for non-EU travelers, filed its claim in an Estonian court. The lawsuit was buried in eu-LISA's 2025 financial accounts , published in July, with no mention of who was being sued. The Financial Times has since named the three companies after obtaining letters exchanged with the agency. In a statement to The Register , eu-LISA confirmed it had initiated proceedings "in line with the Agency’s responsibility to protect the EU’s financial interests." "The proceedings concern the system’s development phase and have no impact on its current operation. EES (entry exit system) is fully operational," the agency said, declining to discuss the ongoing case. The EES was supposed to be ready in 2022 yet wasn't live until October 2025 and was only fully operational from April. Travelers have since had to contend with hours-long airport queues and fingerprint scanners that reportedly struggle with sweaty fingers. Behind the scenes, things weren't going much better, with the consortium and eu-LISA spending years arguing over missed deadlines, financial penalties and who was to blame. IBM Belgium and Atos Belgium were already arguing over penalties back in October 2021, when they disputed a fine from eu-LISA and pointed to the COVID-19 pandemic and other factors beyond their control as reasons for the delays. By February 2022, the consortium was pushing back against another set of deadlines, warning that the agency's timetable was unrealistic. "Ignoring reality is not prudent and will not help to achieve the plan," the companies wrote, according to the FT. "On the contrary, working with an unrealistic plan will cause frustration for all stakeholders." The consortium also criticized eu-LISA's "overall governance," suggesting relations between the two sides had become rather frosty. The fallout wasn't cheap. The contract had already grown from €142 million to €212 million in 2021, and the delays kept adding to the bill. In its 2022 accounts [PDF], eu-LISA acknowledged difficulties with the consortium and warned of additional costs, with the setbacks also holding up other EU IT projects. By 2023, it had nearly doubled its annual EES budget to €40 million by diverting funds from elsewhere, partly to cover rising hardware and software maintenance costs. The FT also reported that IBM agreed in March 2022 to let eu-LISA withhold certain payments while the dispute over damages was resolved. technology.description: Britain’s Royal Navy has formally commissioned its first uncrewed boat squadron, operating seaborne drones on front-line operations as part of its “Hybrid Navy” strategy. The force says the 1 st Autonomous Squadron officially entered active service on November 5 at a ceremony in Portsmouth Naval Base. It comprises around 180 personnel, about the same as a Type 23 frigate, split into two watches to enable operations around the clock. This active squadron replaces Project Beehive, the navy’s experimental program to build a fleet of autonomous and remotely operated vessels, through which it obtained 20 uncrewed boats from UK-based Kraken Technology Group. The force is understood to be using both Kraken’s K3 Scout, and the SM400 from SYOS Aerospace, known by the Royal Navy as the Rattler. The K3 Scout is an 8.4 m boat capable of 55 knots and can carry a payload of up to 600 kg. It has a range of up to 650 nautical miles and endurance of up to 7 days. The maker describes it as capable of a range of missions, including anti-ship and anti-submarine to detecting and countering other drones and even casualty evacuation. The Rattler boat is 7.2 m and has a 500 kg modular bay, with a range of up to 950 nautical miles. It was used last year in a demonstration during which 5 of the uncrewed boats were remotely-piloted to escort patrol ship HMS Tyne and mine countermeasures mothership HMS Stirling Castle Part of the new squadron’s mission will be to act as pathfinder for drone operations, working on bringing additional types of uncrewed surface vessel (USVs) into fleet service and conducting a range of operations alongside other organizations – both as single vessels and as part of a task group. The “Hybrid Navy” concept was outlined by First Sea Lord General Sir Gwyn Jenkins earlier this year, who made the case that uncrewed vessels would be vital in filling the gaps left by the Royal Navy’s much depleted surface fleet. Speaking at the launch of the autonomous squadron, Fleet Commander Vice-Admiral Steve Moorhouse hailed it as an historic occasion, but warned that the seas are becoming more contested, more dangerous and harder to operate in. “A hybrid navy is about giving our people better tools. The Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers (ESCAPADE) spacecraft launched in November 2025 on the second-ever flight of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket. But rather than head straight to Mars, the two spacecraft dawdled through a looping trajectory . Now, they are back in Earth's neighborhood where they tackled a crucial engine burn unusually close to Earth that — if all goes well — will set them on track for Mars . "No NASA mission has ever done this before," said Rob Lillis, a planetary and space physicist at the University of California, Berkeley and principal investigator of the ESCAPADE mission. "For most missions, it just isn't necessary." That's because traditionally NASA's Mars missions have been carefully choreographed within cosmic launch constraints, leaving Earth during a brief window of planetary alignment that only occurs every 26 months. ESCAPADE was meant to launch in October 2024, when Earth and Mars were favorably aligned, but delays with the New Glenn rocket forced the mission to sit out the precious launch window. Rather than wait to launch this fall, NASA decided to try something new. ESCAPADE mission planners designed a "loitering" orbit , shaped like a kidney bean. It called for the twin probes to loop through that trajectory to be back at Earth in early November 2026, ready to continue on to Mars. The ESCAPADE mission's unique path to reach Mars. After launching in November 2025, the twin ESCAPADE probes looped around the Earth-Sun Lagrange point 2 (L2), in a "loiter" orbit that returned them to Earth in November 2026 where they used our planet's gravity to slingshot themselves to Mars. science.title: Global carbon emissions set to fall in 2026 due to Iran energy shock
science.description: The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz led to a spike in oil prices Anna Ivanova/Alamy Carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels are expected to drop this year for the first time in five years. The slowdown has been partly attributed to the energy shock triggered by the US and Israel’s war on Iran. The conflict, which began in February, led to a jump in oil prices after the Strait of Hormuz, the main trade route for about 20 per cent of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas, was blockaded by Iran in response. This is still affecting petrol prices and household gas bills, and has seen countries around the world turn to alternative fuel types to boost energy security. Advertisement Read more Solar energy is going to power the world much sooner than you think Around 38.2 gigatonnes of CO2 are expected to be emitted in 2026 globally, according to the latest annual Global Carbon Budget – put together by more than 140 researchers. This is a 0.4 per cent decrease on the previous year, largely due to a projected 1.9 per cent fall in emissions from oil. The drop in oil use was partly offset by a 0.6 per cent increase in emissions from coal. Robbie Andrew at climate research group CICERO in Oslo, Norway, one of the report authors, says financial pressures due to the energy shock are likely to have caused the drop in emissions this year, which may turn out to be a “blip”. “On the assumption that there are no further crises, then you’d expect that emissions would bounce back,” says Andrew. The two biggest dips in emissions in the 21st century have been attributed to the covid-19 pandemic, which saw emissions drop by around 6 per cent in 2020, and the global financial crisis, which saw emissions drop around 2 per cent in 2009. The future outlook depends on how long the energy shock lasts, says Andrew, with governments forced to look at the economic case for continuing to subsidise fossil fuels. The rollout of renewable energy also played a part in bringing down carbon emissions. Electric vehicles and solar and wind power are predicted to offset 64 to 79 per cent of increasing emissions from demand growth through to 2028. SHERLOC, SuperCam, and PIXL can detect minerals using various techniques including x-ray fluorescence, Raman, and infrared spectroscopies. As a side benefit of the way SuperCam performs its Raman spectroscopy, it can also study time-resolved luminescence. Normally luminescence occurs over a broad wavelength range (most of Earth’s commercial lighting uses luminescence in some way or another). Two years ago, the SuperCam team was startled to find strong, narrow luminescence peaks at two wavelengths of 692.7 and 694.1 nanometers when they shot a light-colored rock with the laser. This luminescence comes from delayed atomic transitions in chromium atoms present in a corundum mineral structure. SuperCam can time the delay of the atomic transitions via the resulting photons, and so we could verify that this emission came from chromium in corundum. The results were published in Geophysical Research Letters by a team led by Ann Ollila earlier this year, so you can read all about it. The gemstone version of chromium-containing corundum is ruby. Prior to installing SuperCam on Perseverance, we placed a ruby in the laser beam and watched the entire room pulse a brilliant red as SuperCam’s laser beam hit the gemstone; it was extremely bright. While we haven’t found collectable rubies on Mars yet, the little corundum crystals are helping us learn more about Mars’ past. Corundum is a metamorphic and pegmatitic mineral which we would not expect to find on Mars, a planet that lacks plate tectonics. Because we are in a very ancient terrain near the rim of Jezero crater, we can expect some evidence of localized metamorphism. As the first mission in such terrain, we are learning new things. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 9, 1967: NASA launches the Saturn V moon rocket for the first time on Apollo 4, but no astronauts were aboard
science.description: null On Nov. 9, 1967, NASA launched the powerful new Saturn V rocket on its maiden voyage. The Saturn V moon rocket was 363 feet tall. That's taller than the Statue of Liberty! It was the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built at the time (though SpaceX's Starship megarocket has since surpassed it). NASA needed such a powerful rocket to launch astronauts to the moon. However, the first Saturn V launch didn't carry astronauts, because it was only a test flight. During the launch, the rocket created a loud shockwave that surprised nearby observers. The ground shook so hard that it rattled buildings miles away, and all the shaking caused a huge shower of dust and debris NASA's new launch center, the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The mission lasted 8 hours 36 minutes. The rocket carried an uncrewed command module that splashed down in the Pacific Ocean. NASA's first-ever Saturn V rocket launches on its maiden flight from Cape Canaveral, Florida on the uncrewed Apollo 4 test flight on Nov. 9, 1967. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered The launch of Apollo 4 in November 1967 was a turning point for NASA on its path to landing astronauts on the moon. The space agency had bet the moon on its new Saturn V booster, a three-stage heavy-lift rocket designed to fly astronauts in a capsule (as well as their lander) to the moon and back. But the rocket had never been fully tested until the Apollo 4 launch. NASA also needed a new launch site for its Apollo missions. So the agency built Launch Complex 39 at what is now called the Kennedy Space Center, a Florida spaceport that has become the home port for orbital human spaceflight in the United States. But in 1967, no rockets had ever flown from the site. Yet, everything went according to plan. Amazing Apollo 4: NASA's 1st Saturn V Moon Rocket Test Flight in Photos “It was really an expert launching all the way through from lifting off exactly on time to performance of every single stage,” rocket pioneer Wernher von Braun , director of NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, said at the time . The launch came as NASA was on its heels. Just months earlier, on Jan. 27, 1967, the space agency suffered a fatal tragedy when Apollo 1 astronauts Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee died on the launch pad after a fire broke out inside their Apollo command module during a ground test. A view of the Apollo 4 launch after stage separation looking back down at Earth from the Saturn V rocket. science.title: Jupiter and Mars are set for a breathtaking close approach later this week: Here's how to see it
science.description: null Jupiter and Mars will shine side by side in a spectacular close approach in the heart of the constellation Leo on Nov. 15. Here's what you need to know. Mars and Jupiter reach their closest apparent separation in Earth's sky at 9:04 p.m. EST on Nov. 15 (0204 GMT on Nov. 16), according to astronomy website In-The-Sky . The planets will be below the horizon for U.S. stargazers at the moment of their closest approach, but observers can catch the pair rising above the eastern horizon around midnight local time, just a few hours later. Remember: You can discover the exact timings for the rising and setting of the planets above your local horizon using Time and Date's night sky tracker . Jupiter will be the brightest of the pair, when it rises a little over 1 degree from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your little finger held at arm's length against the night sky. The bright star Regulus will glow close at hand, forming the dot of the backward question mark formation of stars that represents the head of the great Lion in the constellation Leo. Celestron StarSense Explorer LT114AZ (Image credit: Celestron) The Celestron StarSense Explorer LT114AZ is a great way to get a closer look at Jupiter, Mars and Saturn. Its 4.5-inch aperture and a high 1000mm focal length delivers good magnification out of the box, plus it's integrated with the StarSense smartphone app, which makes finding those planets so much easier. Check out our full review for more. Mars and Jupiter will be close enough to share the field of view of a pair of 10x50 binoculars and will also make for a spectacular sight through the eyepiece of a telescope when viewed separately as they rise away from the horizon. The gas giant's iconic Great Red Spot will rotate into view in the predawn hours of Nov. 16, and will be visible through a backyard telescope with an aperture of just 4 inches . Using a light green color filter will help increase the visibility of the vast storm, while an orange filter will help bring out detail in the gas giant's sweeping cloud belts. The two planets will appear to gradually drift apart over the coming weeks and won't appear as close again for another 2.5 years in July 2029 , when the two planets appear close together in the constellation Virgo . Be sure to check out our guide to photographing the night sky , along with our picks of the best cameras and lenses for astrophotography if you're interested in following the dance of the planets for yourself. science.title: Are the James Webb Space Telescope's mysterious Little Red Dots actually tiny black holes left over from the Big Bang era?
science.description: null Ever since NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) started observing the early universe, it has been providing almost as many surprises as it has answers. One such surprise are the so-called Little Red Dots, cosmic objects that seemingly disappear completely before the universe is two billion years old. New research suggests that Little Red Dots may actually be connected primordial black holes , tiny black holes born not from dying stars but rather from fluctuations in the density of matter just after the Big Bang, in the earliest moments of cosmic history. Should they exist, primordial black holes would predate stars, galactic dust particles, and elements heavier than hydrogen and helium. Now, researchers have used JWST data to test whether one particular Little Red Dot, known as blackAbell 2744-QSO1 (QSO1), could host a primordial black hole. "A black hole is an object born from the gravitational death of a star. Primordial black holes are a very different story," study team member Valerio De Luca, of the Department of Physics and Astronomy at Johns Hopkins University (JHU) in Maryland, said in a statement . "They come from the physics of the early universe that predates the first stars, when the universe was expanding exponentially in time and space. So the mechanisms for creating primordial black holes are different," De Luca added. Little Red Dots could be the smoking gun of primordial black holes Though scientists have theorized about the existence of primordial black holes since they were first proposed by Stephen Hawking in the 1970s, no hard evidence has presented itself. One of the issues scientists have puzzled over is how to tell the difference between a primordial black hole and a "traditional" or astrophysical black hole formed from the supernova death and collapse of a massive star. "Little Red Dots could surround astrophysical black holes, and most probably many of them do, but they could also be primordial black holes, if primordial black holes exist," De Luca said. "So the question becomes, Which ones are primordial and how can we tell?" De Luca and colleagues turned their attention to QS01, located around 13.1 billion light-years from Earth, which is seen as it was just 700 million years after the Big Bang. What makes this Little Red Dot stand out is the fact that it is almost entirely composed of hydrogen and helium. Because these were the universe's first elements, it could be more unspoiled and primordial than other Little Red Dots. The team modeled how a Little Red Dot like QS01 could form from a primordial black hole. That was necessary because the circumstances under which this could happen would have to be very specific. "There are constraints on primordial black holes from cosmological observations," said team member Loris Del Grosso, also of JHU's Department of Physics and Astronomy. Well, the wait for "Robopocalypse" fans might finally be over, as Oscar winners Ron Howard and Akiva Goldsman have announced they're working on a TV adaptation. It does seem like an eternity since news first broke that Portland-based New York Times bestselling author Daniel H. Wilson’s "Robopocalypse" (Doubleday, 2011) was bought by Steven Spielberg’s DreamWorks SKG for a sci-fi spectacle, with Drew Goddard ("The Martian") brought in to pen the screenplay. That was back in 2009, and since then the story of a rogue AI named Archos and a hearty band of indigenous people in America’s heartland battling to save humanity from extinction has been placed on Hollywood’s back burner. After numerous stalled starts and director Michael Bay getting involved in 2018, "Robopocalypse" was quietly powered down due to script issues, filmmaker scheduling conflicts, and the enormous budget required. But now we have been blessed with the news , first broken by The Hollywood Reporter, that Ron Howard ("Apollo 13," "The Da Vinci Code") and Akiva Goldsman ("A Beautiful Mind," "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds") have taken up the mantle of this chilling sci-fi project to develop as a new TV series. "'Robopocalypse' has all the scale and suspense of a major action story, but what drew me to it are the thought-provoking themes and humanity at its center," Ron Howard shared in a statement.
